AUTHOR: Laradji, IH; Saleh, A; Rodriguez, P; Nowrouzezahrai, D; Azghadi, MR; Vazquez, D
TITLE: Weakly supervised underwater fish segmentation using affinity LCFCN
DATA: DeepFish (FishLoc 3200 images, FishSeg 620 images); SUIM fish class as secondary
D_EV: Experiments: 'It is divided into a training set (n = 1600), a validation set (n = 640), and a test set (n = 960).' (unit not stated)
R_EV: Experiments: 'For both cases we use FishSeg's test set to evaluate the segmentation performance.' (FishLoc and FishSeg are both DeepFish); SUIM trained/tested on its own split
C_EV: no statement found (output by argmax: 'The final output is an argmax between the scores to get the final segmentation labels')
E_EV: Evaluation procedure: 'We also measure the model's efficacy in predicting the fish count using mean absolute error ... Ci is the true fish count for image i'
ARCH: A-LCFCN: ResNet38 backbone + activation branch + affinity branch with random walk; pseudo-mask FCN8 (A-LCFCN+PM)
NOTE: DeepFish predefined split (original: random per-habitat image split 50/20/30); the paper gives only counts, no unit -> D_ALL NR. Training FishLoc images overlapping FishSeg test set were removed ('We have removed training images from FishLoc that overlap with FishSeg's test set for reliable results') -> D3/D4=Y, irrelevant to D_ALL for predefined split. Train-on-FishLoc/test-on-FishSeg is within DeepFish, not external. E1 coded as per-image count MAE vs annotated counts of same images (could be judged a pure detection metric -> E1=없음, E_ALL=N). Limitations explicitly note unknown generalization to other habitats. NIMG = 3200+620.
